description: iSCSI/NFS datastore mounted without CHAP/Kerberos authentication - detected within Storage and surfaced through VMware Aria Operations for Logs. Represents a foothold-establishment signal worth correlating with what follows it.
analytic_story: VMware vSphere Attack & Ransomware Precursor Activity (Aria Catalogue)

data_sources.name: vCenter Server task/event logs
data_sources.description: vpxd task and event stream (VM/host/cluster/permission operations), ingested via the Aria 'VMware - vCenter Server' content pack.

data_sources.name: Datastore / storage events
data_sources.description: Datastore, VMFS, and virtual-disk lifecycle events surfaced through vCenter and ESXi logs.

detection_logic: An iSCSI/NFS datastore mounted without authentication trusts network position alone; on a segment reachable by workload VMs this can allow any host on that segment to mount the same storage.
aria_query: ("iSCSI" OR "NFS") AND ("datastore mounted" OR "target added") AND NOT ("CHAP" OR "Kerberos")
how_to_implement: Ingest Storage activity into VMware Aria Operations for Logs via the relevant VMware content pack ('VMware - vSphere', 'VMware - vCenter Server', or 'VMware - NSX-T' depending on source), then confirm the field names referenced in this query (user, vc_username, src, vm_name, host, principal, etc.) match what your content-pack version and source product actually extract before enabling the alert. Use Aria's UI-native time range, grouping, and threshold functions for any count/burst logic rather than embedding statistics in the query.
known_false_positives: Jump-host/bastion IP changes, VPN re-IP, or a new but legitimate administrative workstation.
investigation_steps: Identify the source IP/user and compare against known-good baselines for that identity.
Check for a subsequent successful login or privileged action from the same identity or source.
Correlate with other catalogue entries for the same actor within a short window.

title: vSphere Replication target reconfigured to unrecognized appliance
description: vSphere Replication target reconfigured to unrecognized appliance - detected within vCenter API and surfaced through VMware Aria Operations for Logs. Represents a high-confidence data-exfiltration signal.
analytic_story: VMware vSphere Attack & Ransomware Precursor Activity (Aria Catalogue)

data_sources.name: vCenter Server task/event logs
data_sources.description: vpxd task and event stream (VM/host/cluster/permission operations), ingested via the Aria 'VMware - vCenter Server' content pack.

detection_logic: vSphere Replication continuously streams VM disk changes to a target site; redirecting the target to an attacker-controlled appliance provides an ongoing, low-noise copy of protected workloads without touching the source VM or its normal backup path.
aria_query: ("vSphere Replication" OR "hbr") AND ("target site" OR "VRMS") AND ("changed" OR "reconfigured")
how_to_implement: Ingest vCenter API activity into VMware Aria Operations for Logs via the relevant VMware content pack ('VMware - vSphere', 'VMware - vCenter Server', or 'VMware - NSX-T' depending on source), then confirm the field names referenced in this query (user, vc_username, src, vm_name, host, principal, etc.) match what your content-pack version and source product actually extract before enabling the alert. Use Aria's UI-native time range, grouping, and threshold functions for any count/burst logic rather than embedding statistics in the query.
known_false_positives: Approved OVF/OVA export for migration, archival, or vendor support requests.
investigation_steps: Identify what left the environment, its destination, and the initiating account.
Treat as a high-priority incident pending confirmation of business authorization.
Review for preceding collection, cloning, or snapshot activity on the same object.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1020: Automated Exfiltration
